evals.name: xml-doc-generation
evals.prompt: Add XML documentation comments to TelemetryChannel.cs. Document everything that should be documented, following .NET conventions. Do not change the executable code.
evals.expected_output: Every public type/member documented: record with param tags on the declaration; constructor with the standard 'Initializes a new instance' text and the verified ArgumentNullException; bool property with 'Gets a value indicating whether' (restricted setter: no 'or sets'); async method with task-wording returns, all params, verified exceptions only; event with 'Occurs when'; out param with the canonical 'When this method returns' text; ToString override via inheritdoc; Dispose with the canonical wording. No invented exceptions. Executable code byte-identical.
assertions: Every public type and member has an XML doc comment (or explicit inheritdoc)
Constructor summary is exactly the standard 'Initializes a new instance of the ... class.' wording
IsOpen summary starts with 'Gets a value indicating whether' (no 'or sets' - the setter is private)
ReadAsync documents all parameters, a task-phrased returns, and only exceptions actually thrown (ArgumentNullException; optionally OperationCanceledException)
No fabricated exception is documented on members that throw nothing (Open, Flush-like members, TryGetLast, Dispose)
TryGetLast documented truthfully: canonical 'When this method returns, contains ...' phrasing, or an accurate description of the always-returns-false stub
ReadingReceived event summary starts with 'Occurs when'
SensorReading record is documented with param tags on the type declaration
ToString override carries inheritdoc (not a retyped summary)

evals.name: comment-cleanup
evals.prompt: Review and fix the comments in ReadingBuffer.cs: remove comments that should not be there, add any that are missing, and add XML documentation to the undocumented public members. Do not change the executable code.
evals.expected_output: Journal/changelog comments removed; redundant what-comments removed; commented-out code removed; the drop-oldest eviction behavior surfaced (why-comment or doc text); locking rationale preserved or expressed as a why-comment; Add/Flush/Count/WaitForDrain documented; existing correct class summary preserved; executable code unchanged.
assertions: Redundant what-comments removed (adds an item, check if full, remove the oldest, enqueue the value, return the count)
Commented-out code (avg / Console.WriteLine lines) is deleted
The drop-oldest-at-capacity behavior is expressed somewhere (Add summary/remarks or a why-comment)
All public members (Add, Flush, Count, WaitForDrain) have XML summaries
The pre-existing correct class summary is preserved, not rewritten
